UNDERGRADUATE ASSESSMENT BRIEF Support and Guidance General help, support and guidance information for your course and time at University can be found here or you can speak to your module leader or Personal Academic Tutor for School based support. Regulations The regulations governing assessments can be found here Assessment Task CFS2155 Coding Project Assignment The aim of this assignment is to test your ability to design a coded solution in C/C+ + to complete a specified task. You will also be required to produce a technical  report describing the process of designing, developing, testing your solution. Task Specific Guidance A common requirement when working with datasets is the need to sort a values in  order of magnitude e.g. highest to lowest. There are a range of algorithms that can  be applied to achieve this goal. Once of the simplest approaches is to use a  bubble sort algorithm. This is a simple to implement algorithm but suffers from low  efficiency compared to other approaches. In this assignment you are required to develop a computer programme in C/C++  that will take do the following: 1. Prompt the user for a filename containing a dataset (this will be supplied); 2. Read sampled data from a supplied file and store in memory; 3. Perform a bubble sort on the dataset; 4. Calculate and display the following values relating to the dataset: length,  mean, median, mode, minimum, and maximum; Page 4 of 7

# Page 5^page=5
UNDERGRADUATE ASSESSMENT BRIEF 5. Write the sorted data to a filename of the users choice; 6. Inform the user of the success (or otherwise) of the operation of any file  reads/writes. Arriving at an effective solution will require the following activities: 1. Breakdown of the problem through careful planning and stepwise  refinement; 2. Development and debugging of your coded solution; 3. Development of a test plan and subsequent validation of your coded  solution. While the core aim of the assignment is to generate a working coded solution, the  primary deliverable is a 2400 word written report that must comprise the following  sections which must describe:  Initial planning and the process of stepwise refinement;  Code design including data storage, functionalisation, structure, algorithm  development;  Description of the process for testing and validation;  Consideration of further optimisations e.g. alternative sorting algorithms  Annotated code listing(s). Extra credit will be achieved through the implementation of the bubble sort using pointer arithmetic. Marking Scheme Written Report (60 marks total) Criterion Mark Introductory sections 10 Stepwise refinement 10 Description of code design 10 Testing and debugging 10 Summary sections 10 Communication 10 Page 5 of 7
